# OSWorld1

Open-ended tasks on a real Ubuntu desktop: Chrome, LibreOffice, GIMP, VLC, VS Code, Thunderbird, the OS and workflows across them, each in a VM of its own.

## Nullius limitations

- Nullius standard: the original is OSWorld's own agents at the repository's main branch (its last release, v0.1.16, predates them), one per value of the Agent option, M3's harness the default: each script (scripts/python/run_*.py) as published, on one task per unit, asking one of the models it is published with, scored by the upstream's DesktopEnv.evaluate on the VM's final state. Its arguments are its own documented invocation's (README, docstring or scripts/bash wrapper) on the docker provider, one environment per run; every other setting is its default (upstream-settings.json says each, agents.json holds the arguments).
- Each unit runs in a VM of its own, which the upstream's docker provider gives 4 CPU cores and 4 GB of memory: one unit at a time is the minimum, and more run side by side (-j) as far as the machine allows. Their VMs start one after another, each once the one before has its container running: the upstream's docker provider fails a start that waits more than 10 s for its port lock. Docker is needed on the machine, and /dev/kvm for speed: without it the upstream runs the VM unaccelerated. The machine also needs the system libraries the driver's environment loads (libgl1, libglib2.0-0, libx11-6, libxext6 and libgomp1, OpenCV's among them), and the VM image is best fetched before the first run: docs/benchmarks/osworld1-machine.md sets a machine up step by step.
- A task's outcome can depend on the machine's speed: the upstream's runners wait fixed times, not for the desktop (60 s after a task is set up, then a fixed pause after each action, from none to 10 s by agent), so a slow or loaded machine can show the agent a desktop that has not caught up, or run out of the task's time limit. Compare scores from machines of similar speed and load.
- MiniMax M3 is reached through OpenRouter's Anthropic Messages endpoint (minimax/minimax-m3), its key held by the relay. The thinking option is adaptive by default, as run_multienv_m3.py's own documented invocation sets it; off is the agent's code default. In the model setup, a reply that is not in M3's <tool_call> format is asked again by M3Agent, three times at most, then the step does nothing: a model that does not answer in that format makes many calls for few steps. The thinking option is M3's alone.
- Agents offered (12): M3, PromptAgent, Claude computer use, GPT-5.4, OpenAI CUA, Qwen-CUA, OS-Symphony, EvoCUA, AutoGLM-OS, AutoGLM-OS with vision, Mano and Muse Spark. Models are sent as OpenRouter names them (served_as): GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.4, Claude, Qwen and M3 run on OpenRouter; OpenAI CUA asks a model only OpenAI serves (computer-use-preview), so it needs the OpenAI provider, where the OpenRouter names of the others do not resolve; EvoCUA, AutoGLM, Mano and Muse Spark need the model server their authors run (the custom provider). Whether OpenRouter carries Anthropic's computer-use beta tool, and the Responses API's computer tool and server-side state that GPT-5.4 uses, is untested. OS-Symphony's web searcher drives a second VM of its own when it searches, so such a unit can take two. Claude computer use and OpenAI CUA import the upstream's AWS manager whatever the provider, which refuses to load without AWS_REGION, AWS_SUBNET_ID and AWS_SECURITY_GROUP_ID: the driver sets us-east-1 and placeholders, and no AWS call is made on docker.
- Agents not offered: UI-TARS (all three scripts), DART-GUI, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, Aguvis, OWL and o3 fail every task at this commit, before any model call: lib_run_single passes reset() a vm_ip their agents do not accept. Both Kimi scripts fail at import: their package imports modules the commit does not have; so does CoAct: its vendored autogen imports diskcache, which the upstream's lock does not install. Pointer (AWS Bedrock), Gemini (Google's native API), GBOX, AGI and UiPath (private services), GTA1, Maestro, OpenCUA and Aguvis (literal addresses), Mobile-Agent-v3 and GUI-OWL 1.5 (Aliyun OSS uploads, aws or DashScope's native API), Seed (an SDK the lock lacks), AWorld (a framework the upstream does not ship) and VLAA-GUI (Bedrock, DashScope and Gemini together) cannot send their calls through the relay. upstream-settings.json gives each one's file and line.
- No agent of Nullius runs it yet: it needs agent.computer/v1, defined ahead of its kit. Only the original and model setups and the null control run.
- No reference control: OSWorld publishes no solutions. The null control is Nullius's: the upstream's run_single_example with an agent whose one action is DONE, then the upstream's evaluator on the untouched VM. It runs in the score step, which Nullius limits to 600 s per task.
- Datasets: Without Google Drive comes first and is the default, since the 8 Google Drive tasks of All tasks (the upstream runners' default) need account credentials the upstream does not ship. The Windows tasks (examples_windows) are not run.
- 49 tasks of Without Google Drive ask for a proxy. M3, Qwen-CUA, Claude computer use, AutoGLM-OS (both) and Mano run them without the proxy setup (their default, or Qwen-CUA's off, since its default needs a proxy provider's credentials); PromptAgent, GPT-5.4, OpenAI CUA, OS-Symphony, EvoCUA and Muse Spark hard-code it on, so those tasks are set up through the upstream's DataImpulse settings, whose credentials are placeholders, and fail or run without a working network.
- Unpinned upstream downloads, as the upstream names them: the Ubuntu VM image from Hugging Face (xlangai/ubuntu_osworld, its main revision), fetched once into the upstream's docker_vm_data, and the happysixd/osworld-docker image, pulled when missing. The driver's environment is the upstream's uv.lock, torch included: several GB, installed once per machine. The lock is the upstream's only pinned dependency list; it predates the upstream's latest pyproject.toml changes and lacks packages its README's requirements.txt adds (mcp, daytona and others), each of them imported only by another VM provider or agent. A run from requirements.txt resolves its versions on the day it is installed (the anthropic and openai SDKs among them), so its software can differ from these runs'.
- M3's runner retries a task after an infrastructure error up to 3 times within the unit, and its watchdog restarts a worker whose model calls stop for 900 s; the other agents keep their own retries. A task stopped at Nullius's limit (2 hours for a setup, 600 s for the null control's score) has its processes killed and its VM containers removed by the driver: each unit hands the provider its VM image through a link in its own folder, so its containers, a second VM of an agent's own included, are the ones that mount it. The upstream's own signal handling leaves them running, and so does a script that crashes after starting its VM: the driver removes them whenever the script ends. They carry no Nullius label.
- Each task keeps the upstream's own output in its trial folder: a screenshot per step, traj.jsonl, runtime.log, the API logs and recording.mp4, often hundreds of MB.
